title: Reproducible SEM analyses
summary: A reproducible analysis lets anyone obtain the same numbers from the same model, data, settings and seed, and SEM Lab's exported scripts check that agreement automatically.

body.text: [[reproducibility]] means that the same model, data, settings and code produce the same numbers. For SEM that requires the model specification, the prepared data (or a description of how to obtain them), all estimation settings, the [[random-seed]] and number of bootstrap draws, and the software versions.

SEM Lab exports an R script (cSEM for PLS, lavaan for CB-SEM) or a Python script with the analysed data. The PLS export and the browser engine agree to about 1e-12; the Python script compares its numbers with the app's result and prints whether they agree within tolerance. Keep the exported folder with your paper's materials.

items: Fix the seed and B before running and never select among seeds.
Record which cases and items were removed and why (Data Lab keeps a transformation log).
Share code and, where licences and privacy allow, data; otherwise share a synthetic dataset with the same structure.

body.text: Different programs can legitimately differ: some apply individual sign-change corrections in the bootstrap or use other defaults. Agreement is expected only when model, data, options and seed are identical.

mistake.title: Rerunning until the numbers look better
mistake.text: Changing settings, seeds or exclusions after seeing results, without reporting it, makes the analysis irreproducible in spirit even if every single run is reproducible.

tryIt.task: Run the TAM example, then export the analysis as a Python or R script from the Results page. Read the README in the exported folder and identify where the seed and the settings are stored.

checks.question: Which information is needed to reproduce a bootstrap confidence interval exactly? Select all that apply.

options.text: The seed and the number of draws
The model specification and estimation settings

options.feedback: Correct. A single changed case changes the resamples.

options.text: The screen resolution of the analyst's computer
options.feedback: Display settings have no influence on the computation.

checks.question: Your exported script reports a largest difference of 0.03 from the app. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The script ran on different data or options than the app analysed, for example an edited CSV.
options.feedback: Correct. Identical inputs agree within the script's tolerance (1e-9 for PLS, 1e-6 for CB-SEM).
Floating-point differences are many orders of magnitude smaller than .03.
With the same seed both draw the same resamples.
